title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and deduplicate matrices
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Motivation: our GitHub Actions configuration has grown ad-hoc over time with separate workflows for lint, unit/integration tests, and release automation that largely duplicate job matrices and setup steps. This increases maintenance burden, leads to inconsistent node/tool versions across repos, and causes a lot of duplicated runner time. This PR consolidates the lint, test, and release workflows into a small set of reusable templates and a unified workflow that: 1) deduplicates matrix definitions (node versions, OS, python versions where applicable), 2) centralizes cache keys and actions versions, 3) standardizes Node->Node 20 for build/test jobs, and 4) keeps the release automation separate but driven by the same templates to preserve security boundaries.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced .github/workflows/ci-unified.yaml that runs lint, unit tests, integration smoke, and bundling checks in one workflow with conditional release dispatch.
- Added .github/workflows/templates/ci-job-template.yml and templates/release-job-template.yml to encapsulate common steps (checkout, cache, setup-node, restore-cache, install, test, upload-artifacts).
- Replaced three workflows (lint.yaml, test.yaml, release.yaml) with the unified workflow and templates. The release workflow is now a thin dispatcher that uses the secure release template.
- Standardized Node to 20.x across JS/TS jobs, updated actions to pinned versions, and consolidated caching semantics to reduce redundant installs.
- Improved matrix usage: OS x node versions x package-manager is now driven by a single matrix definition with an allowlist for slow integration combinations.
- Added lightweight self-checks and a canary path to run a full matrix only on main and release branches.

Testing and rollout:
- Verified lint & unit test jobs in feature branches (see CI runs below).
- Ran full matrix in a staging branch and compared runtime (median) against previous workflows: ~28% reduction in total runner minutes for pull-request CI across mono-repo packages.
- Kept release artifacts/release branch protections intact. Release dispatch still requires release-team approval and uses the same GPG-signing steps as before.

Backward compatibility & migration notes:
- Existing branch protections and required checks will be updated by ops to reference the new workflow names.
- If a repo relies on an older node version for a specific package, add an override in that package's workflow config (documented in .github/README-CI.md added in this PR).

Checklist: 
- [x] Add templates and unified workflow
- [x] Migrate lint/test/release callers to new workflow
- [x] Validate cache keys and reduce duplication
- [x] Run full matrix in staging and compare metrics
- [x] Update CI docs in .github/README-CI.md

Impact: reduces CI cost and maintenance by removing duplicated steps and centralizing upgrades. No functional changes to runtime code. Release process preserved.

Notes: there was one flaky integration job on the first run (postgres setup timing). I added a short retry wrapper and bumped the integration timeout; subsequent runs passed.

Related Linear: ENG-4521, INFRA-884.
commits: refactor(ci): add ci-unified.yaml and retire lint/test/release workflows
docs(ci): add README-CI.md describing templates and migration
chore(ci): pin actions and standardize node -> 20.x
fix(ci): add retry for postgres setup in integration job
review_comments: Samir Gupta: Nice cleanup. Two asks: 1) can we keep a short-lived compatibility matrix for node 16/18 for critical packages? 2) please add metrics for median runner minutes in the PR description.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added a short allowlist for node 16/18 on flagged packages and included a runtime delta in the description (28% reduction).
Ava Rodriguez: Please ensure the release dispatcher still requires the release-team label and GPG signing — I see the dispatcher file, but verify the secret usage.
Priya Natarajan (author): Confirmed: release-dispatcher preserves label guard and uses the same GPG_SECRET reference; added an explicit comment to the release template.
ci_checks: integration-smoke (failed on first run - postgres timeout; rerun passed)
release-dry-run (skipped on PR, executed on merge to main)
release_notes: Consolidate CI workflows: introduces unified CI workflow and reusable templates, standardizes Node to 20.x, reduces CI runner minutes. No runtime behavior changes.
